post_title: Normal map slide to others pattern pieces
post_details: Hello, Sometimes I see a slide of normal maps from different seamline or quilted lines to other garment pieces. You can see on the placket on the 3D window and rendering. Does anyone know how to fix it? BR Roei

Hi there, I am wondering why my neckband/hem goes this puffy? I dropped particle distance to 5, thickness is 0. The hem is folded edge and the neckband is two piece pattern segment. Please let me know if you need any additional information.

comments.comment_body: It looks like you need to add an internal line where the "fold" is. The added internal line will change the shape of the mesh so it will be able to fold smoothly. Once you add an internal line you can assign it a fold angle so it will look like a nice crisp fold. These videos HERE and HERE you may find helpful
If I am not wrong there already is an internal line? Photo included.

You are correct. Thank you for the additional photo. What looks like what may be happening is that part of of the fold back has gone too far. In the 3D Toggle If you switch from Thick Textured Surface to Textured Surface you will probably see "grey back" areas poking out the front. If you Reset 3D arrangement of the Sleeve and then refold the hem this should help. Just remember then When using the Fold arrangement tool in the 3D Tool bar you don't need to fold the hem all of the way, just most of the way. Then when you turn on Simulation the gravity/sewing will will take it the rest of the way

Hi there, it's so much better. It seems like I pushed the fold to far. But still can there is a small puff, you can see it by the picture - is there a way to make it completely flat like it's pressed? Thank you so much for helping me!:)

I can see that you are using the GPU simulation. It behaves a bit weirdly with layers and creates that puffy effect. If you switch to "Normal (Default)" or "Fitting (Accurate Fabric)" it should flatten nicely.

Check your pattern pieces fabric thickness for collision also. The default setting can make a folded (back to back) folded simulation quite thick if it is set to 2.5mm for each strip in the property editor. By checking the &gt additional collision offset for the pattern piece in the property editor and adjusting that factor (reduce) you will get the fabric to sit closer in a pressed seam. Sometimes for the visual (render) you might need to decide on treating 'knife' edge areas on the construction differently to 'production construction'. So this is maybe where your marketing image and forking your garment (eg: history save state) into a 'render beauty' 3D model might happen. For example in CLO3D you can use 'thick render and curvature' along with additional thickness render for any pattern piece to give the appearance of double folded pattern piece. And so for some seams you might even trim the sleeve construction in that zone and reduce it to a thin seam strip of single (unfolded) seam trim with additional render thickness applied to the total thickness you want in that local area for a crisp simulation. In other words &gt for the final marketing render image you might need to break with the Manufactured construction in order to get the VFX visual just how you want.

another option I see often is: to make that foldback piece a separate pattern piece. sew it to the opening edge. ( and sew the other edge to an internal line that you add to the sleeve pattern) select that edge seam and "edit sewing " in property editor change it to the seam type to "turned" &amp and it will look flat like its pressed. also be sure to place the foldback piece on in the 3d window by " superimpose under" for great placement.

post_title: Squaring off perpendicular to edges - help!
post_details: Hi, I want to know how to square off from edges (for example, squaring off the first part of the neckline from centre front) and keep them squared off when grading. When you hold shift to drag out a bezier curve, it does not create a guideline on the x or y axis like Adobe Illustrator. It creates guidelines based on something else (not sure what), but it's not helpful. Is there a way to drag the bezier curves out with guides on the x or y axis? Secondly, when grading, first you have to convert all the beziers to curve points. This is fine, but it means that lines that have been squared off do not retain that shape when graded. That means the grade starts going more and more off-course, creating divots or points at edges that should remain squared off. Is there a way to make the grade function retain the perpendicular corner? (Note: the perpendicular corner tool does not do anything useful here) I hope someone can help me!

comments.comment_body: Hi 902622733903 When grading we do recommend using Curve Points instead of the Bezier Handles. -When holding shift to drag the bezier handle the XY axis is based off of where the handle was located when you clicked on it and not where the Segment Point is. -For squaring something off at a right angle or similar you would want to have a Segment Point there and then Grade from that Segment Point. Have you taken a look at our Youtube channel which has several Grading videos HERE

post_title: Topstitch won't appear during the simulation.
post_details: Hi everyone! I was wondering if there is a way to see the topstitch while simulating. I'm using a chain as OBJ for this, I noticed when I use the obj as "Texture" it shows up but it's flat. But as soon as I try to use the OBJ with its real volume it only shows up when simulation is off. Thanks in advance! Vicky

comments.comment_body: Hi 13331650244377 When using an OBJ topstitch they will not appear when simulation is turned on. This is to keep simulation speed up. So you will only see topstitch when Simulation is off

The need to see the simulation whilst it is operating is possibly 'semantic'. It's nice to see elements in all their detail as you simulate - but is it needed given the simulation is determined by physical collision outside most of your immediate control ? In other words it's going to do what it will do irrespective of user interference until that simulation stops using the assembly constraints you place on the garment (for control). It is what it is - however you may tweak and adjust the result using tools after it has simulated. The reduced mesh acts like a 'object' placeholder with boundaries determined by the objects offset, so in many respects the speed of the collision is the most useful element &gt then tweak after. You may also 'solidify' a pattern object prior to simulation if you want to hold a specific chain drape, that gives you some control over fixing that prior to more detailed simulation, where you can pull it around during the simulation to interact with cloth - yet hold the chains basic shape.

post_details: After drafting and sewing a pocket to my jacket, I hit simulate to attach it. Then, this large, abstract form appears and sucks my entire outfit to it. I've never experienced this kind of error before. Any ideas what's happening?

comments.comment_body: Hi 13545994094105 What attaching the pocket did you use Superimpose before simulating? Superimpose allows items like pockets to move 99% of the way so that during simulation you get minimal collision like you see above. You can find a video of this in action HERE

A good way to reduce collision or assembly performance issues is to use the arrange pattern piece close to the avatar or assembly garment (blue dot), this will cut down on potential assembly simulation errors associated with pattern placement. Also you may need to make sure you don't have the pattern flipped (normals) and that the collision offset is set to the default for the pattern piece. So maybe just run through a checklist for that pattern element.
